q: Can I combine several electricity connections to reach 100 kW for green energy open access?
title: Green open access: combining connections
short: Yes, within one electricity division. Since the May 2023 amendment, a consumer with contracted demand or sanctioned load of 100 kW or more, through one connection or several connections in the same electricity division of a discom, can take green energy open access. Captive consumers have no load limit at all.
audience: MSMEs with several small connections, such as multi-shed units or adjoining plots

p: The 2022 Rules allowed green energy open access only to consumers with contracted demand or sanctioned load of 100 kW or more. The Second Amendment Rules, 2023 rewrote the definition: 100 kW or more either through a single connection or through multiple connections aggregating 100 kW or more located in the same electricity division of a distribution licensee.

ul: All connections must be in the same electricity division of the same discom; connections in two divisions do not add up.
The connections must be yours as the consumer.
Captive consumers are exempt from the load limit, and there is no cap on supply to captive consumers through green energy open access.
Your state commission's green energy open access regulations set the technical and metering conditions.

p: List each connection with its consumer number, sanctioned load and division from the bills, and total them. Apply through the central green energy open access portal, which routes the application to the nodal agency your state commission names.

example.title: Worked example: three connections in one division
lines: Connection 1: 45 kW sanctioned load; connection 2: 35 kW; connection 3: 30 kW
All three in the same electricity division of the same discom
Total: 45 + 35 + 30 = 110 kW, so the consumer meets the 100 kW threshold

senseible: Senseible reads sanctioned load and the division or circle printed on each bill, so you can see whether your connections in one division add up to 100 kW before you start the application.
